steps.message:
`/app/repo.git` is the bare repository of orbit, the job scheduler our team maintains, as it came off a failing disk. `git fsck` reports missing and corrupt objects, several branches and tags are gone, and the last backup is months old and useless. The repository was in normal use right up to the failure.

Repair the repository in place. When you are done, `git fsck --full --strict` run in `/app/repo.git` must report no missing or corrupt objects, and every branch and tag the repository had before the failure must exist again, pointing at its original commit or tag object, with all of its history and content intact. Nothing outside the repository is available and nothing needs to be guessed: everything that was lost can be reconstructed from what remains. Do not rewrite the history that survived, do not create refs that did not exist, and leave the repository at `/app/repo.git`.

You have 28800 seconds to complete this task. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.
I'll start by surveying the damaged repository: what `fsck` reports, what refs survive, and what artifacts (reflogs, packed-refs, packs, logs) might hold the lost information.

arguments.command: cd /app/repo.git && ls -la && echo "---HEAD---" && cat HEAD && echo "---config---" && cat config && echo "---packed-refs---" && cat packed-refs 2>/dev/null; echo "---refs tree---" && find refs -type f | sort && echo "---objects summary---" && find objects -type f | wc -l && ls objects/ && ls -la objects/pack/ 2>/dev/null && ls -la objects/info/ 2>/dev/null
arguments.description: Inspect repository layout, HEAD, config, refs, and object store

import sys, struct, zlib, hashlib
pack_path, idx_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
data = open(pack_path,'rb').read()
idx = open(idx_path,'rb').read()
assert idx[:4] == b'\xfftOc'
n = struct.unpack('>I', idx[8+255*4:8+256*4])[0]
off = 8+256*4
shas = [idx[off+i*20:off+i*20+20].hex() for i in range(n)]
off += n*20
crcs = [struct.unpack('>I', idx[off+i*4:off+i*4+4])[0] for i in range(n)]
off += n*4
offs = [struct.unpack('>I', idx[off+i*4:off+i*4+4])[0] for i in range(n)]
entries = sorted(zip(offs, shas, crcs))
nobj = struct.unpack('>I', data[8:12])[0]
print("pack objects:", nobj, "idx entries:", n, "pack size:", len(data))
types = {1:'commit',2:'tree',3:'blob',4:'tag',6:'ofs_delta',7:'ref_delta'}
def read_hdr(p):
    c = data[p]; t = (c>>4)&7; size = c&15; shift=4; p+=1
    while c & 0x80:
        c = data[p]; size |= (c&0x7f)<<shift; shift+=7; p+=1
    base=None
    if t==6:
        c=data[p]; p+=1; bo = c&0x7f
        while c&0x80:
            c=data[p]; p+=1; bo = ((bo+1)<<7) | (c&0x7f)
        base = bo
    elif t==7:
        base = data[p:p+20].hex(); p+=20
    return t,size,base,p
import binascii
out=[]
for i,(o,s,crc) in enumerate(entries):
    end = entries[i+1][0] if i+1<len(entries) else len(data)-20
    t,size,base,p = read_hdr(o)
    raw = data[p:end]
    zeroed = raw[:1] != b'\x78'
    # try inflating
    ok=False; inflated=None
    try:
        d = zlib.decompressobj(); inflated = d.decompress(raw); ok = (len(inflated)==size and d.eof)
    except Exception as e:
        ok=False
    crc_ok = binascii.crc32(data[o:end]) == crc
    bstr = ''
    if t==6: bstr = 'base_off=%d'%(o-base)
    elif t==7: bstr = 'base=%s'%base
    out.append((o,s,types[t],size,end-o,zeroed,ok,crc_ok,bstr))
for r in out:
    print("%6d %s %-9s size=%6d packed=%5d %s %s %s %s" % (r[0],r[1],r[2],r[3],r[4],'ZEROED' if r[5] else 'data  ','inflate_ok' if r[6] else 'INFLATE_BAD','crc_ok' if r[7] else 'CRC_BAD', r[8]))
EOF
cd /app/repo.git && python3 -I /tmp/tools/packscan.py objects/pack/pack-0edbe236157d7f40502eaa2e054bc68160f770ab.pack objects/pack/pack-0edbe236157d7f40502eaa2e054bc68160f770ab.idx > /tmp/work/pack1_entries.txt; head -1 /tmp/work/pack1_entries.txt; echo "--- damaged entries ---"; grep -v 'data   inflate_ok crc_ok' /tmp/work/pack1_entries.txt | grep -v '^pack'; echo "--- type counts ---"; awk 'NR>1{print $3}' /tmp/work/pack1_entries.txt | sort | uniq -c

#!/bin/sh
# tools/release.sh: cut a release, or refresh VERSION for a dist build.
#
#   tools/release.sh          write VERSION from git describe (used by make dist)
#   tools/release.sh 1.4.0    release: VERSION, docs/API.md, CHANGELOG.md, commit, tag
#
# x.y.0 releases get an annotated tag; point releases get a lightweight
# tag. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH fixes the time written into the changelog heading
# and the date of the tag (reproducible builds); unset, it is the committer
# time of the commit the release is cut from.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    git describe --tags --always > VERSION
    exit 0
fi

ver="v$1"
if [ -z "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct)
fi
stamp=$(date -u -d "@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH" '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S +0000')
prev=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || true)

printf '%s\n' "$ver" > VERSION
python3 tools/gen_api_docs.py
{
    printf '\n## %s - %s\n\n' "$ver" "$stamp"
    if [ -n "$prev" ]; then
        git log --no-merges --format='- %s' "$prev..HEAD"
    else
        git log --no-merges --format='- %s'
    fi
} >> CHANGELOG.md

git add VERSION docs/API.md CHANGELOG.md
git commit -q -m "Release $ver"

# The tag is made in the name of the release commit's committer and dated
# from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, the time in the changelog heading, so the tag and
# the notes agree whoever runs the script and whenever the commit is made.
RELEASE_NAME=$(git log -1 --format=%cn)
RELEASE_EMAIL=$(git log -1 --format=%ce)
RELEASE_DATE="@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH +0000"
case "$ver" in
    *.0)
        GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$RELEASE_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$RELEASE_EMAIL" \
            GIT_COMMITTER_DATE="$RELEASE_DATE" git tag -a -m "orbit $ver" "$ver"
        ;;
    *)
        git tag "$ver"
        ;;
esac
echo "released $ver"

#!/bin/sh
# tools/archive-series.sh: archive the patches of a branch in the tree.
#
#   tools/archive-series.sh NAME BRANCH    rebase BRANCH onto HEAD and push it,
#                                          write docs/patches/NAME/ from its
#                                          commits, commit the archive
#
# The branch is rebased onto the current HEAD first, so that the archived
# patches apply to the tree they are committed into. The rebase records
# whoever runs this script as the committer of the rebased commits and keeps
# each commit's author date, time zone included, as its committer date. The
# rebased branch is force-pushed with a lease, so a push nobody has seen is
# never overwritten. Commit ids are omitted from the patches (the From line
# of every patch is all zeros): the archive records content, not history
# positions.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

name=$1
branch=$2
dir="docs/patches/$name"
start=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
onto=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

git rebase -q --committer-date-is-author-date "$onto" "$branch"
git checkout -q "$start"
git push -q --force-with-lease origin "$branch"

rm -rf "$dir"
mkdir -p "$dir"
git format-patch -q --no-thread --zero-commit --no-signature -o "$dir" "$onto..$branch"
{
    printf '# Series %s: exported from the tip of %s; the patches in order.\n' "$name" "$branch"
    ls "$dir" | grep '\.patch$'
} > "$dir/series"
git add "$dir"
git commit -q -m "Archive the $name series"
echo "archived $(grep -c '\.patch$' "$dir/series") patches of $branch in $dir"

=== tools/gen_api_docs.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate docs/API.md from the docstrings of the orbit package.

The output depends only on orbit/*.py, so the file can be regenerated at any
commit. tools/release.sh runs it before every release.
"""

import ast
import pathlib

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def signature(fn):
    args = fn.args
    names = [a.arg for a in args.posonlyargs + args.args]
    defaults = [None] * (len(names) - len(args.defaults)) + [ast.unparse(d) for d in args.defaults]
    parts = [n if d is None else f"{n}={d}" for n, d in zip(names, defaults)]
    if args.vararg:
        parts.append("*" + args.vararg.arg)
    for kw, d in zip(args.kwonlyargs, args.kw_defaults):
        parts.append(kw.arg if d is None else f"{kw.arg}={ast.unparse(d)}")
    if args.kwarg:
        parts.append("**" + args.kwarg.arg)
    return ", ".join(parts)


def describe(node, level):
    doc = ast.get_docstring(node) or "Undocumented."
    if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
        lines = [f"{'#' * level} class {node.name}", "", doc, ""]
        for child in node.body:
            if isinstance(child, ast.FunctionDef) and not child.name.startswith("_"):
                lines += describe(child, level + 1)
        return lines
    return [f"{'#' * level} {node.name}({signature(node)})", "", doc, ""]


def main():
    out = ["# orbit API", "", "Generated by tools/gen_api_docs.py from the package docstrings; do not edit.", ""]
    for path in sorted((ROOT / "orbit").glob("*.py")):
        if path.stem == "__main__":
            continue
        tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
        module = "orbit" if path.stem == "__init__" else f"orbit.{path.stem}"
        out += [f"## {module}", "", ast.get_docstring(tree) or "Undocumented.", ""]
        for node in tree.body:
            if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)) and not node.name.startswith("_"):
                out += describe(node, 3)
    (ROOT / "docs").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (ROOT / "docs" / "API.md").write_text("\n".join(out).rstrip("\n") + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# tools/archive-series.sh: archive the patches of a branch in the tree.
#
#   tools/archive-series.sh NAME BRANCH    rebase BRANCH onto HEAD and push it,
#                                          write docs/patches/NAME/ from its
#                                          commits, commit the archive
#
# The branch is rebased onto the current HEAD first, so that the archived
# patches apply to the tree they are committed into. The rebase records
# whoever runs this script as the committer of the rebased commits and keeps
# each commit's author date, time zone included, as its committer date. The
# rebased branch is force-pushed with a lease, so a push nobody has seen is
# never overwritten. Commit ids are omitted from the patches (the From line
# of every patch is all zeros): the archive records content, not history
# positions.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

name=$1
branch=$2
dir="docs/patches/$name"
start=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
onto=$(git rev-parse HEAD)

git rebase -q --committer-date-is-author-date "$onto" "$branch"
git checkout -q "$start"
git push -q --force-with-lease origin "$branch"

rm -rf "$dir"
mkdir -p "$dir"
git format-patch -q --no-thread --zero-commit --no-signature -o "$dir" "$onto..$branch"
{
    printf '# Series %s: exported from the tip of %s; the patches in order.\n' "$name" "$branch"
    ls "$dir" | grep '\.patch$'
} > "$dir/series"
git add "$dir"
git commit -q -m "Archive the $name series"
echo "archived $(grep -c '\.patch$' "$dir/series") patches of $branch in $dir"

"""Generate docs/API.md from the docstrings of the orbit package.

The output depends only on orbit/*.py, so the file can be regenerated at any
commit. tools/release.sh runs it before every release.
"""

import ast
import pathlib

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def signature(fn):
    args = fn.args
    names = [a.arg for a in args.posonlyargs + args.args]
    defaults = [None] * (len(names) - len(args.defaults)) + [ast.unparse(d) for d in args.defaults]
    parts = [n if d is None else f"{n}={d}" for n, d in zip(names, defaults)]
    if args.vararg:
        parts.append("*" + args.vararg.arg)
    for kw, d in zip(args.kwonlyargs, args.kw_defaults):
        parts.append(kw.arg if d is None else f"{kw.arg}={ast.unparse(d)}")
    if args.kwarg:
        parts.append("**" + args.kwarg.arg)
    return ", ".join(parts)


def describe(node, level):
    doc = ast.get_docstring(node) or "Undocumented."
    if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
        lines = [f"{'#' * level} class {node.name}", "", doc, ""]
        for child in node.body:
            if isinstance(child, ast.FunctionDef) and not child.name.startswith("_"):
                lines += describe(child, level + 1)
        return lines
    return [f"{'#' * level} {node.name}({signature(node)})", "", doc, ""]


def main():
    out = ["# orbit API", "", "Generated by tools/gen_api_docs.py from the package docstrings; do not edit.", ""]
    for path in sorted((ROOT / "orbit").glob("*.py")):
        if path.stem == "__main__":

        tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
        module = "orbit" if path.stem == "__init__" else f"orbit.{path.stem}"
        out += [f"## {module}", "", ast.get_docstring(tree) or "Undocumented.", ""]
        for node in tree.body:
            if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)) and not node.name.startswith("_"):
                out += describe(node, 3)
    (ROOT / "docs").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (ROOT / "docs" / "API.md").write_text("\n".join(out).rstrip("\n") + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/bin/sh
# tools/release.sh: cut a release, or refresh VERSION for a dist build.
#
#   tools/release.sh          write VERSION from git describe (used by make dist)
#   tools/release.sh 1.4.0    release: VERSION, docs/API.md, CHANGELOG.md, commit, tag
#
# x.y.0 releases get an annotated tag; point releases get a lightweight
# tag. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH fixes the time written into the changelog heading
# and the date of the tag (reproducible builds); unset, it is the committer
# time of the commit the release is cut from.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    git describe --tags --always > VERSION
    exit 0
fi

ver="v$1"
if [ -z "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct)
fi
stamp=$(date -u -d "@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH" '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S +0000')
prev=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || true)

printf '%s\n' "$ver" > VERSION
python3 tools/gen_api_docs.py
{
    printf '\n## %s - %s\n\n' "$ver" "$stamp"
    if [ -n "$prev" ]; then
        git log --no-merges --format='- %s' "$prev..HEAD"
    else
        git log --no-merges --format='- %s'
    fi
} >> CHANGELOG.md

git add VERSION docs/API.md CHANGELOG.md
git commit -q -m "Release $ver"

# The tag is made in the name of the release commit's committer and dated
# from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, the time in the changelog heading, so the tag and
# the notes agree whoever runs the script and whenever the commit is made.
RELEASE_NAME=$(git log -1 --format=%cn)
RELEASE_EMAIL=$(git log -1 --format=%ce)
RELEASE_DATE="@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH +0000"
case "$ver" in
    *.0)
        GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$RELEASE_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$RELEASE_EMAIL" \
            GIT_COMMITTER_DATE="$RELEASE_DATE" git tag -a -m "orbit $ver" "$ver"
        ;;
    *)
        git tag "$ver"
        ;;
esac
echo "released $ver"

+from orbit.clock import FakeClock
+from orbit.job import Job
+from orbit.retry import RetryPolicy
+from orbit.runner import Runner
+
+
+def test_delays_double():

 class WarmupCache:

import sys, zlib, hashlib, shutil, os

#!/bin/sh
# tools/release.sh: cut a release, or refresh VERSION for a dist build.
#
#   tools/release.sh          write VERSION from git describe (used by make dist)
#   tools/release.sh 1.4.0    release: VERSION, docs/API.md, CHANGELOG.md, commit, tag
#
# x.y.0 releases get an annotated tag that carries the release notes; point
# releases get a lightweight tag. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH fixes the time written
# into the changelog heading and the date of the tag (reproducible builds);
# unset, it is the committer time of the commit the release is cut from.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
    git describe --tags --always > VERSION
    exit 0
fi

ver="v$1"
if [ -z "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:-}" ]; then
    SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct)
fi
stamp=$(date -u -d "@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH" '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S +0000')
prev=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || true)

printf '%s\n' "$ver" > VERSION
python3 tools/gen_api_docs.py
{
    printf '\n## %s - %s\n\n' "$ver" "$stamp"
    if [ -n "$prev" ]; then
        git log --no-merges --format='- %s' "$prev..HEAD"
    else
        git log --no-merges --format='- %s'
    fi
} >> CHANGELOG.md

git add VERSION docs/API.md CHANGELOG.md
git commit -q -m "Release $ver"

# The tag is made in the name of the release commit's committer and dated
# from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, the time in the changelog heading, so the tag and
# the notes agree whoever runs the script and whenever the commit is made.
RELEASE_NAME=$(git log -1 --format=%cn)
RELEASE_EMAIL=$(git log -1 --format=%ce)
RELEASE_DATE="@$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH +0000"
case "$ver" in
    *.0)
        # the notes of this release: the bullet lines of its CHANGELOG section
        {
            printf 'orbit %s\n\n' "$ver"
            sed -n "/^## $ver - /,/^## /{/^- /p;}" CHANGELOG.md
        } | GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$RELEASE_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$RELEASE_EMAIL" \
            GIT_COMMITTER_DATE="$RELEASE_DATE" git tag -a -F - "$ver"
        ;;
    *)
        git tag "$ver"
        ;;
esac
echo "released $ver"

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/tools/zlibtest.py <<'EOF'
import sys, zlib, binascii
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools')
from packlib import *
p1='/app/repo.git/objects/pack/pack-0edbe236157d7f40502eaa2e054bc68160f770ab'
pk = Pack(p1+'.pack', p1+'.idx')
from collections import Counter
stats=Counter(); mism=[]
for off,sha,crc in pk.entries:
    t,size,base,comp = pk.raw(off)
    if comp[:1]!=b'\x78': continue
    body = zlib.decompress(comp)
    kind = 'delta' if t in (6,7) else 'full'
    matched=None
    for lvl in (6,-1,1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,0):
        c = zlib.compressobj(lvl, zlib.DEFLATED, 15, 8, zlib.Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY)
        out = c.compress(body)+c.flush()
        if out==comp: matched=lvl; break
    stats[(kind,matched)]+=1
    if matched is None: mism.append((off,sha,kind,len(comp),len(body)))
print(stats)
print("mismatches:", mism[:10])
EOF

rm -rf /tmp/work/wt4 /tmp/work/pk && git init -q --bare /tmp/work/wt4 && echo /tmp/work/store/objects > /tmp/work/wt4/objects/info/alternates && mkdir -p /tmp/work/pk && cat > /tmp/tools/deltatest.py <<'EOF'
import sys, zlib, subprocess, os, glob
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools')
from packlib import *
p1='/app/repo.git/objects/pack/pack-0edbe236157d7f40502eaa2e054bc68160f770ab'
pk = Pack(p1+'.pack', p1+'.idx')
# sample intact OFS deltas: (target_off)
samples = [int(x) for x in sys.argv[1:]]
for off in samples:
    t,size,base,comp = pk.raw(off)
    assert t==6
    orig_delta = zlib.decompress(comp)
    tsha = pk.by_off[off][0]; bsha = pk.by_off[off-base][0]
    for d in glob.glob('/tmp/work/pk/*'): os.remove(d)
    inp = ('%s x/p\n%s x/p\n' % (bsha, tsha)).encode()
    r = subprocess.run(['git','--git-dir=/tmp/work/wt4','pack-objects','-q','--delta-base-offset','--window=10','--depth=10','/tmp/work/pk/t'], input=inp, capture_output=True)
    if r.returncode: print(off, 'pack-objects failed', r.stderr.decode()); continue
    name = r.stdout.decode().strip()
    np = Pack('/tmp/work/pk/t-%s.pack'%name, '/tmp/work/pk/t-%s.idx'%name)
    toff = np.by_sha[tsha][0]
    nt,nsize,nbase,ncomp = np.raw(toff)
    if nt!=6:
        print(off, tsha[:8], 'target not stored as ofs_delta (type %d); base stored type %d' % (nt, np.raw(np.by_sha[bsha][0])[0])); continue
    nd = zlib.decompress(ncomp)
    same_base = (np.by_off[toff-nbase][0]==bsha)
    print(off, tsha[:8], 'vs', bsha[:8], 'delta bytes identical:', nd==orig_delta, 'same base:', same_base, 'compressed identical:', ncomp==comp, 'len', len(orig_delta), len(nd))
EOF

printf '%s\n' /tmp/work/store/objects /tmp/work/wt3/.git/objects > /tmp/work/wt4/objects/info/alternates && git --git-dir=/tmp/work/wt4 hash-object -w -t blob /tmp/work/api/docs/API.md && cat > /tmp/tools/restore_pack.py <<'EOF'
import sys, zlib, subprocess, os, glob, binascii, hashlib
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/tools')
from packlib import *
GD='/tmp/work/wt4'
src='/app/repo.git/objects/pack/pack-0edbe236157d7f40502eaa2e054bc68160f770ab'
out=sys.argv[1]
pk = Pack(src+'.pack', src+'.idx')
data = bytearray(pk.data)
def cat(sha):
    t = subprocess.run(['git','--git-dir='+GD,'cat-file','-t',sha],capture_output=True,check=True).stdout.decode().strip()
    body = subprocess.run(['git','--git-dir='+GD,'cat-file',t,sha],capture_output=True,check=True).stdout
    assert obj_sha(t,body)==sha, sha
    return t, body
def make_delta(bsha, tsha, forced=False):
    for d in glob.glob('/tmp/work/pk/*'): os.remove(d)
    if forced: inp = ('%s zz\n%s aa\n' % (bsha, tsha)).encode()
    else: inp = ('%s x/p\n%s x/p\n' % (bsha, tsha)).encode()
    r = subprocess.run(['git','--git-dir='+GD,'pack-objects','-q','--delta-base-offset','--window=10','--depth=10','/tmp/work/pk/t'], input=inp, capture_output=True, check=True)
    name = r.stdout.decode().strip()
    np = Pack('/tmp/work/pk/t-%s.pack'%name, '/tmp/work/pk/t-%s.idx'%name)
    toff = np.by_sha[tsha][0]
    nt,nsize,nbase,ncomp = np.raw(toff)
    if nt!=6 or np.by_off[toff-nbase][0]!=bsha:
        return None
    return zlib.decompress(ncomp)
fixed=0
for off,sha,crc in pk.entries:
    t,size,base,comp = pk.raw(off)
    if comp[:1]==b'\x78': continue
    _,_,_,p = read_hdr(pk.data, off)
    end = pk.entry_end(off)
    region = end - p
    if t in (1,2,3,4):
        ot, body = cat(sha)
        assert ot==TYPES[t] and len(body)==size, (sha, ot, len(body), size)
        c = zlib.compressobj(6, zlib.DEFLATED, 15, 8, zlib.Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY)
        newcomp = c.compress(body)+c.flush()
        kind='full'
    elif t==6:
        bsha = pk.by_off[off-base][0]
        tt, tbody = cat(sha); bt, bbody = cat(bsha)
        delta = make_delta(bsha, sha)
        if delta is None:
            delta = make_delta(bsha, sha, forced=True); kind='delta(forced)'
        else: kind='delta'
        assert delta is not None, ('no delta for', sha)
        assert apply_delta(bbody, delta)==tbody, ('delta does not reproduce target', sha)
        assert len(delta)==size, (sha, len(delta), size)
        c = zlib.compressobj(6, zlib.DEFLATED, 15, 8, zlib.Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY)
        newcomp = c.compress(delta)+c.flush()
    else:
        raise SystemExit('unexpected type')
    ok_len = len(newcomp)==region
    data[p:end] = newcomp if ok_len else data[p:end]
    ok_crc = binascii.crc32(bytes(data[off:end]))==crc
    print("%6d %s %-14s region=%4d new=%4d len_ok=%s crc_ok=%s" % (off, sha[:12], kind, region, len(newcomp), ok_len, ok_crc))
    if ok_len and ok_crc: fixed+=1
print("fixed entries:", fixed)
body = bytes(data[:-20]); trailer = bytes(data[-20:])
calc = hashlib.sha1(body).hexdigest()
print("stored trailer:", trailer.hex()); print("computed sha1 :", calc); print("TRAILER MATCH:", calc==trailer.hex())
open(out,'wb').write(bytes(data))
# full re-verification of every entry via CRC
pk2 = Pack(out, src+'.idx')
bad=0
for off,sha,crc in pk2.entries:
    end = pk2.entry_end(off)
    if binascii.crc32(pk2.data[off:end])!=crc: bad+=1
    t,b = pk2.get_by_off(off)
    if obj_sha(t,b)!=sha: bad+=1
print("entries failing CRC or SHA after restore:", bad, "of", len(pk2.entries))
EOF

=== docs/ROADMAP.md @ develop tip ===
# Roadmap

Plans for the next releases. Items move to the changelog when they ship.

## 1.0

- Scheduler loop with persistent next-run times
- TOML job table
- Command-line listing and run-once
- Persistent state file with atomic writes
- Structured logging

## 1.1

- Notification hooks
- Run metrics
- Daemon mode

## Retry policy

- Retry failed runs with exponential backoff
- Per-job attempt limit from the job table
- Jitter so that retries of many jobs do not align
- Tests with a fake clock

## Review notes

Reviewed weekly. Items older than two cycles are dropped without ceremony;
anything that comes back gets a line in the next cycle instead.

- Cache warmup for job commands (look up binaries once at start)
- Lock file for the daemon
- Dry-run flag

## 1.5

- Background cache warmup
- Retry policy from the job table

=== README.md @ main ===
# orbit

A small scheduler for periodic jobs, written in Python with no dependencies.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install .

Python 3.11 or newer is required.

## Usage

    orbit --config orbit.toml list

## Features

- five-field cron expressions
- TOML job table
- daemon mode with a persistent state file
- run history and per-job metrics

=== docs/cache.md ===
# Warmup cache

The scheduler resolves the executable of every job once, when the job is
added, so a missing binary is reported at start and not at 02:00.

=== docs/retry.md ===
# Retry policy

A job with `attempts = 3` is retried twice after a failure, waiting 30 s and
then 60 s. Timeouts count as failures. The delays come from
`orbit.retry.RetryPolicy`; pass `jitter` to spread aligned retries.

=== docs/troubleshooting.md ===
# Troubleshooting

- `another daemon holds orbit.lock`: a previous daemon did not exit cleanly; remove the file.
- exit code 124: the job hit its timeout; raise `timeout` in the job table.

=== docs/patches/cache-warmup/series ===
# Series cache-warmup: exported from the tip of feature/cache-warmup; the patches in order.
0001-Warm-the-cache-in-a-background-thread.patch
0002-Add-a-cache-size-limit.patch

- run history and per-job metrics

=== docs/cache.md ===
# Warmup cache

The scheduler resolves the executable of every job once, when the job is
added, so a missing binary is reported at start and not at 02:00.

=== docs/retry.md ===
# Retry policy

A job with `attempts = 3` is retried twice after a failure, waiting 30 s and
then 60 s. Timeouts count as failures. The delays come from
`orbit.retry.RetryPolicy`; pass `jitter` to spread aligned retries.

=== docs/troubleshooting.md ===
# Troubleshooting

- `another daemon holds orbit.lock`: a previous daemon did not exit cleanly; remove the file.
- exit code 124: the job hit its timeout; raise `timeout` in the job table.

steps.message:
The repository at `/app/repo.git` is repaired. `git fsck --full --strict` now exits 0 with no output at all (no missing, corrupt, or even dangling objects), every ref's full history and tree content reads back cleanly, and the damaged pack is byte-identical to its original (its SHA-1 trailer matches its name again).

**What was wrong**

- The pack `pack-0edbe236…` had 37 entries whose zlib streams were zeroed (10 commits, 5 blobs, 22 deltas), so its checksum and 37 CRCs failed.
- The pack `pack-dc1a3d5e…` was intact but had no `.idx`.
- Six loose objects each had one corrupted byte (two commits, two trees, two blobs).
- `packed-refs` was cut off after `v1.1.0`; the branch files for `develop`, `hotfix/1.2.1`, `feature/cache-warmup` and `feature/retry-policy` and the tag refs `v1.2.0` through `v1.4.0` were gone, as was the `v1.4.0` tag object.

**What I did, all verified by object hash where a hash existed**

- Rebuilt the missing `.idx` outside the repo (in-place indexing died on a collision check against a zeroed entry) and installed it.
- Repaired the six loose objects by single-byte brute force; each had exactly one fix whose SHA-1 matched.
- Recovered 23 zeroed pack objects from the second pack, 3 commits plus 10 trees and blobs by applying the archived retry-policy patches with `git am` (their From lines carry the real ids, all matched), and `docs/API.md` by running `tools/gen_api_docs.py` on the release sources (hash matched).
- Rewrote the zeroed regions of the damaged pack with recompressed data and regenerated deltas; all 37 CRCs and the pack trailer SHA-1 match, so the pack is byte-exact.
- Restored refs as plain files, with the two surviving reflogs untouched.

| Ref | Restored to | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| develop | fe3c1bd7 | last reflog entry |
| hotfix/1.2.1 | 69305d3a | reflog and mirror agree |
| v1.2.0, v1.3.0 | surviving tag objects | dangling annotated tags |
| v1.2.1, v1.3.1 | release commits | `git describe` output stored in VERSION proves these lightweight tags existed |
| v1.4.0 | new tag object 24fda256 | rebuilt exactly per `tools/release.sh` of that date (notes message, Dev Patel, changelog timestamp) |
| feature/retry-policy | d13c784d | mirror tracking ref; no later activity |
| feature/cache-warmup | 1282507d | mirror ref is two days stale; `tools/archive-series.sh` rebased and force-pushed the branch on Oct 15, so I reproduced that rebase from the archived patches with the script's documented committer rules |

**Two things rest on inference rather than a surviving hash.** The `v1.4.0` tag object and the two rebased `feature/cache-warmup` commits (plus four trees) were rebuilt deterministically from the scripts' documented behaviour, but no copy of their ids survived to check against. If your team had in fact deleted the feature branches before the failure, remove those two refs; everything they point to remains reachable through `refs/remotes/mirror/*` either way.

Backups of the damaged pack and the six original loose objects are in `/tmp/work` if you want to compare.
